data.title: Asian gasoline margin plunges to over three-year lows on ample supplies
data.description:
By Mohi Narayan

Asian gasoline margins plummeted around 69% this week as abundant supplies from China and the Middle East weighed on crack spreads, traders and analysts said on Thursday.

The refining profit, or crack, (GL92-SIN-CRK) for gasoline shrank to $2.67 per barrel over Brent crude, the lowest level since October 2023, from a record peak of $50.53 on October 1.

"Increased Chinese exports are further weighing on the sentiment," Stuti Jhunjhunwala, oil market analyst at Energy Aspects, said.

Gasoline crack spreads usually shrink heading into the northern hemisphere's winter, when fuel demand falls, however, this year they hit record highs on a tight supply outlook, caused by the Middle East war, Russia's export ban and lower inventories at key trading hubs.

The margins fell to six-month lows at the end of October and have been on a downward trend since amid hopes of higher supplies.

"Plenty of supplies from China and year-end destocking causing the fall," a Dubai-based light distillate trader said.

Meanwhile, gasoline imports at the Singapore trading and blending hub tanked 69% to 67,000 tons (about 566,000 barrels) in the week to November 18, while exports rose about 13% on-week to roughly 459,000 tons, government data showed.

The top supplier was China at about 50,000 tons, while the top destination for exports was Australia at 111,000 tons.

data.title: RBA board member sees pockets of strong demand in economy, weakness elsewhere
data.description:
An Australian central bank board member said on Friday that she sees pockets of strong demand in the economy but weakness elsewhere against the backdrop of a massive global oil supply shock.

Speaking at an event in Canberra, Renee Fry-McKibbin, an external board member at the Reserve Bank of Australia said trade-offs in monetary policy are difficult, balancing inflation and employment, and board members can disagree on how to manage them.

data.title: Fed's Paulson says higher rates needed to combat inflation
data.description:
Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia President Anna Paulson said on Thursday the US central bank will need to raise rates again because inflation is too high in an otherwise robust economy.

"I see growth that's strengthened and I see a labor market being at full employment, and so it's clear that inflation needs to be...the priority" of monetary policy making right now, Paulson said after a speech in New York. "And the way we bring inflation down is by having higher rates" and the Fed has "more tightening to do," the official said.

data.title: Fed Cuts Pay Raises for Regional-Bank Staff — WSJ
data.description:
By Nick Timiraos

The Federal Reserve's board in Washington approved a much smaller budget for across-the-board pay increases at the central bank's 12 regional banks, according to people familiar with the matter.

Regional-bank officials told their employees on Wednesday that the funds approved for salary increases would result in minimum annual raises of 1% across the system next year, down from 3% this year. Board staff in Washington, who received raises of 1% this year, will receive similar increases next year. The Fed system employed around 24,000 people in 2024.

The moves will leave many employees with wage gains that don't keep pace with inflation.

In at least one case, bank leaders told employees that the board's decision didn't reflect the bank's assessment of employee performance. The Fed didn't provide a reason for the changes to the annual budget, which was the first under new Chairman Kevin Warsh. Bloomberg News earlier reported the pay guidance.

While employees were told to expect smaller overall pay gains than in prior years, the board approved a somewhat larger pool of funds for incentive pay and retention bonuses for workers in positions facing higher demand, according to a person familiar with the matter.

The Fed has taken other steps in recent years to control administrative expenses. Last year, then-Chair Jerome Powell announced a 10% staff reduction over several years, accomplished largely through early retirements or attrition. Months later, Fed officials announced plans to reduce the Fed's division of supervision and regulation in Washington by around 30%.

The decision highlights a tension for the Fed, which sets pay for its employees outside the federal civil-service system. Its leaders have faced pressure from the Trump administration to manage costs, with Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent last year faulting the system for "institutional bloat." Many civilian federal workers received a 1% raise this year and are slated for a pay freeze next year.

In an introductory note to the system's rank-and-file employees sent in June, Warsh said he expected to have "open, clear-eyed discussions of Fed strategies, policies, and operations" over the coming quarters.

Some employees described the decision as out of character for the Fed system, where the board and the regional banks usually work toward consensus. The quasi-private regional banks have cultivated a loyal, mission-driven culture to compete with banks and private-sector firms for economists, bank examiners and technology specialists. But they have faced renewed attention from the board as it seeks to streamline duplicative operations to control costs, stirring concerns inside the system about the boundaries between the board and the regional banks.

Write to Nick Timiraos at Nick.Timiraos@wsj.com

data.title: New leaders to take helm at law firm Sullivan & Cromwell
data.description:
By Sara Merken

Sullivan & Cromwell said on Thursday that Robert Giuffra, who is a personal lawyer for US President Donald Trump, and Scott Miller will step down as leaders of the New York law firm in 2028, with partners Carsten Berrar and Sharon Nelles slated to take over.

  • The pair will become vice chairs of the prominent Wall Street firm in January 2027, and replace Guiffra and Miller as co-chairs the following year.

  • Giuffra and other lawyers at Sullivan & Cromwell have represented Trump in the Republican president's bid to overturn his criminal conviction in New York for concealing a $130,000 hush money payment ​to porn star Stormy Daniels.

  • The leadership transition comes Democrats are poised to take full control of the US Congress next year.

  • Berrar is managing partner of the firm's Frankfurt office and co-head of its global capital markets group, while Nelles is managing partner of its litigation group. Both are on Sullivan & Cromwell's management committee.

  • Nelles has represented clients including Airbnb, Boeing and Goldman Sachs, and Berrar has advised on deals for clients including Praxair, Delivery Hero and Porsche SE, the firm said.

  • “Careful and deliberate succession planning and a commitment to stewardship have been central to S&C’s success since our founding in 1879,” Giuffra and Miller said in a statement.

  • Giuffra and Miller, who have led the firm since 2022, will become senior chairs in 2028 and continue working with clients, the firm said.

  • Partner Ivan Deutsch will also become a vice chair focusing on firm administration.

data.title: Ringleader pleads guilty to $100 million US jewelry heist
data.description:
By Steve Gorman

The ringleader in a spate of truck burglaries pleaded guilty on Thursday to a federal robbery charge for his role in stealing roughly $100 million worth of jewelry from an armored vehicle five years ago in California, considered the largest such heist in US history, prosecutors said.

Carlos Victor Mestanza Cercado, 33, an Ecuadorean national arrested two years ago in Panama during a layover on a flight from Guatemala to his home country, was one of seven men indicted on charges of robbing a Brink's truck at a highway rest stop north of Los Angeles on July 11, 2022.

The armored vehicle was plundered while carrying 73 sacks of precious gems and fine jewelry from a major exhibition in the San Francisco Bay area to a Southern California storage facility.

Mestanza and his accomplices, who had followed the jewelry shipment in multiple vehicles for 300 miles (480 km) while coordinating by cellphone, broke through the locks of the armored truck while it was parked at a rural Kern County rest stop and got away with 24 bags of treasure, authorities said.

The stolen collection of fine gold, diamonds, rubies, emeralds and luxury watches were valued at approximately $100 million, marking the largest US jewelry heist on record, according to the US Attorney's Office in Los Angeles.

Under an agreement with prosecutors signed earlier this month, Mestanza pleaded guilty to a single count of interference with commerce by robbery, a felony punishable by up to 20 years in prison, in return for prosecutors dropping several other charges he faced. Sentencing was set for April 15.

In addition to the jewelry heist, Mestanza admitted to taking part with his co-defendants in the highway robberies of electronics being shipped by several trucks in March 2022. A statement from the U.S. Attorney's Office in Los Angeles announcing his guilty plea described Mestanza as "the lead defendant in the case."

Three of Mestanza's co-defendants are scheduled for trial in March 2027 in federal court in Los Angeles. Two others remain at large and a seventh accused member of their gang has been deported.

It was not clear from court documents whether any of the stolen jewelry from the heist was ever recovered.

data.title: EMVision Medical Devices Awarded $3m Grant to Expand Brain Scanner into Trauma Care
data.description:
EMVision Medical Devices has been awarded a $3 million federal grant to develop and clinically test its portable First Responder brain scanner for suspected traumatic brain injury (TBI).

The funding will support a second proposed clinical application for the device, building on its existing development work to detect bleeding associated with stroke.

The grant was awarded under round 19 of the Australian government’s Cooperative Research Centres Projects (CRC-P) program.

EMVision expects project work to begin in the first quarter of 2027, with clinical study activation planned for the second half of that year.

Second Clinical Application

The project will investigate whether First Responder can identify bleeding inside the skull following a head injury, using diagnostic technology being developed for stroke assessment.

The battery-powered, non-ionising scanner is designed to be carried to patients, potentially allowing paramedics and clinicians to assess suspected brain bleeding before hospital arrival.

Patients with suspected TBI currently commonly require hospital computed tomography (CT) imaging to establish whether a bleed is present, particularly when symptoms are subtle.

Testing will compare scans from patients with suspected injuries against hospital CT or magnetic resonance imaging, with researchers measuring preliminary detection accuracy and assessing device safety.

EMVision will explore possible concussion assessment applications, although the immediate focus remains detection of traumatic bleeding.

Wider Portable Scanning Market

Falls are a leading cause of TBI, particularly among older people, making aged care a potential additional setting for the technology alongside emergency services and military operations.

EMVision estimates that more than 50 million people sustain TBI worldwide each year, with about 200,000 events annually in Australia.

In the US, an estimated 2.8 million TBI-related emergency department visits, hospitalisations, and deaths occur annually, compared with approximately 800,000 strokes.

The company estimates adding trauma assessment could more than double the potential number of scans per First Responder under its planned per-scan consumables model, although this is not a revenue forecast.

Third CRC-P Grant Award

The new award marks EMVision’s third under the program, and is separate from the $3m CRC-P grant the company received in 2025 for the emu Regional Benefits Study.

CRC-P requires matched cash or in-kind contributions, while the latest funding remains conditional on agreements with the Commonwealth and project partners.

Metro North Hospital and Health Service and Titan Prehospital Innovation are participating, with EMVision targeting completion of the agreements in the coming months.

The company plans to establish clinical protocols and obtain ethics approvals in the first half of 2027 before commencing patient recruitment and preliminary validation work.

Strong TBI Foundation

“A single portable device that can detect a bleed in minutes at the point of care—for both stroke and trauma—and bring treatment and transfer decisions forward to the moment of first contact is a particularly compelling proposition for patients and healthcare systems,” managing director Scott Kirkland said.

“Fresh blood has the same dielectric properties whether it comes from a stroke or a head injury, and as a result, the bleed detection capability we are building into our First Responder for stroke, alongside acute ischaemia detection, gives us a strong foundation for TBI.”

The company intends to use the clinical findings to determine the sensitivity and specificity of its trauma detection algorithms and guide subsequent regulatory studies.

First Responder remains an investigational device and is not approved for detecting TBI or bleeding inside the skull in any jurisdiction, with any future trauma indication dependent upon satisfactory clinical evidence and regulatory clearance.

data.title: Soybean basis offers flat to higher
data.description:
Basis offers for soybeans shipped by barge to US Gulf Coast export terminals were steady to up on Thursday. Basis offers for corn were flat to mixed.

  • CIF soybean barges loaded in December were offered at 113 cents a bushel over Chicago Board of Trade January futures , rising 1 cent. Offers for soybean barges loaded in January also rose 1 cent, to 116 cents a bushel over January futures.

  • CIF corn barges loaded in December traded at 96 cents over CBOT December corn futures, while barges loaded in the last half of December traded at 99 cents over December corn futures.

  • CIF corn barges loaded in November were offered at 89 cents over December corn futures, falling 2 cents. Barges loaded in January were offered at 98 cents over futures, rising 1 cent.

  • The US Department of Agriculture reported exporters sold 200,844 metric tons of soybeans to Mexico for 2026/27 delivery.

  • The Busan section of the Korea Feed Association (KFA) in South Korea purchased up to 63,000 metric tons of animal feed corn in a private deal on Wednesday without issuing an international tender, European traders said on Thursday.

  • CBOT December corn ended 3-1/2 cents higher at $4.39 per bushel after hitting $4.32-1/4, the contract's lowest since June 30.

  • CBOT January soybeans settled down 9-1/4 cents at $12.07-1/2 per bushel.

data.title: Guardforce AI Announces 1-for-40 Reverse Share Split and Adoption of Dual-Class Share Structure
data.description:
Class A Ordinary Shares Expected to Begin Trading on a Split-Adjusted Basis on November 24, 2026

NEW YORK, NY , Nov. 19, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Guardforce AI Co., Limited (“Guardforce AI” or the “Company”) , a technology-enabled service company providing solutions in Agentic AI, smart solutions in automation, robotics, and secured logistics, today announced that, pursuant to the approval of its board of directors and the approval of its shareholders at the Company’s reconvened extraordinary general meeting held on Tuesday, November 3, 2026 at 11:00 a.m. (Hong Kong standard time) (November 2, 2026 at 10:00 p.m. Eastern Time), it is effecting a 1-for-40 share consolidation of its ordinary shares (the “Reverse Share Split”), together with a related capital reduction, share subdivision and re-designation of its share capital into Class A ordinary shares and Class B ordinary shares. The Reverse Share Split and the related capital reduction, share subdivision and re-designation of its share capital are subject to registration by the Registrar of Companies of the Cayman Islands. The Reverse Share Split and re-designation became effective on November 11, 2026, upon registration by the Registrar. The Company’s Class A ordinary shares are expected to begin trading on a split-adjusted basis on the Nasdaq Capital Market at the opening of trading on November 24, 2026. The Class A ordinary shares will replace the existing ordinary shares and continue to trade under the symbol “GFAI” and will have a new CUSIP number G4236L146.

Reverse Share Split Details

Every forty (40) issued and unissued ordinary shares, par value US$0.12 each, will be consolidated into one (1) share, par value US$4.80 each. Immediately afterwards, the par value of each issued share will be reduced to US$0.001 through a capital reduction, and each authorized but unissued share of par value US$4.80 will be subdivided into 4,800 shares of par value US$0.001 each. The Company’s authorized share capital will remain US$36,000,000. The reduction in par value will create a distributable reserve that the Company may use for purposes permitted by law and its articles of association, including to offset accumulated losses.

The Reverse Share Split will reduce the number of issued and outstanding ordinary shares from approximately 31,958,004 to approximately 799,233, subject to adjustment for the rounding up of fractional entitlements described below.

Fractional Shares

No fractional shares will be issued in connection with the Reverse Share Split. Any registered shareholder who would otherwise be entitled to a fractional share will receive one additional whole share, rounded up to the nearest whole number. No cash will be paid in lieu of fractional shares. Shareholders who hold their shares through a broker, bank or other nominee should contact that nominee, as the treatment of fractional entitlements in their accounts is subject to the nominee’s procedures.

Warrants and Other Securities

Proportionate adjustments will be made to the number of shares issuable and the exercise price under the Company’s outstanding warrants, options and other convertible securities in accordance with their terms. Following the Reverse Share Split, each outstanding PIPE warrant will be exercisable for 1/160 of one ordinary share, and the exercise price will be adjusted to US$186 per post-consolidation share.

Re-designation into Class A and Class B Ordinary Shares

Immediately following the Reverse Share Split, the Company’s issued and outstanding shares will be re-designated on a one-for-one basis into approximately 719,199 Class A ordinary shares and approximately 80,034 Class B ordinary shares, each with a par value of US$0.001. The Company’s authorized share capital will be re-designated into 34,500,000,000 Class A ordinary shares, 500,000,000 Class B ordinary shares and 1,000,000,000 preferred shares, each with a par value of US$0.001. The Company’s shareholders also approved the adoption of the Second Amended and Restated Memorandum of Association and the Third Amended and Restated Articles of Association to reflect the new share structure.

Each Class A ordinary share carries one (1) vote and each Class B ordinary share carries twenty (20) votes on all matters submitted to a vote at general meetings of the Company. Class A and Class B ordinary shares vote together as a single class. Holders of Class B ordinary shares may convert them into Class A ordinary shares on a one-for-one basis at any time. Class B ordinary shares convert automatically upon transfer to any person that is not an affiliate of the holder or an existing holder of Class B ordinary shares. Class A ordinary shares are not convertible into Class B ordinary shares.

Immediately following the re-designation, all Class B ordinary shares will be held by Lei Wang, the Company’s Chairwoman and Chief Executive Officer. As a result, Ms. Wang’s voting power will increase from approximately 10% to approximately 69% of the total voting power of the Company's outstanding shares.

Exchange Agent and Shareholder Actions

VStock Transfer, LLC is acting as exchange agent for the Reverse Share Split. Registered shareholders who hold their shares in book-entry form do not need to take any action; their accounts will be adjusted automatically. Shareholders who hold their shares through a broker, bank or other nominee will have their positions adjusted by that nominee. Holders of physical share certificates will receive instructions for exchanging their certificates from the exchange agent and should not submit certificates until requested to do so.

Equity Incentive Plan Amendment

Shareholders also approved Amendment No. 2 to the Guardforce AI Co., Limited 2022 Equity Incentive Plan, which increases the maximum number of shares available for grant from 15% of the issued and outstanding ordinary shares to 20% of the issued and outstanding Class A ordinary shares at the time of grant.

About Guardforce AI Co., Limited

Guardforce AI Co., Limited is a technology-enabled service company built on real-world service operations, trusted client relationships, and commercial smart service solutions. With its legacy secured logistics business as the operating foundation, the Company is expanding its first commercial growth curve through Smart Solutions across retail, hospitality, security, and other service environments, while building AI-native services as its second strategic growth engine. For more information, visit www.guardforceai.com, or X (formerly Twitter): @Guardforceai.

data.title: Here's what India's mutual funds bought and sold in October
data.description:
India's Mutual Funds remained net buyers in October, buying equities worth ₹42,500 crore, in a month before the turnaround began for the markets, pushing the banking index to a record high. Foreign institutional investors (FIIs) sold ₹34,200 crore, as per Nuvama Alternative and Quantitative Research. Following are all the major additions, reductions, new purchases and exits by some of the mutual funds in October, as per Nuvama Alternative:

SBI MF | India's largest fund house bought shares of ITC (₹1,380 crore), Jio Platforms (₹803 crore), and Hindustan Aeronautics (₹793 crore). It trimmed its stake in financials and auto companies like Bajaj Finance (₹718 crore), Kotak Mahindra Bank (₹716 crore), and Bajaj Auto (₹700 crore). Fresh purchases were made in new listings like Paras Healthcare, while the fund made a complete exit from Rainbow Children, Lodha and L&T Finance.

Aditya Birla Sun Life MF | The fund house bought shares worth ₹583 crore in Jio Platforms during the month of October. Persistent Systems was also a big buy for the fund with a purchase of ₹330 crore. Tata Group's Trent was also on the buy list of the fund this month (₹247 crore). It reduced stake in Bharti Airtel (₹753 crore), Reliance Industries (₹453 crore), and Infosys (₹390 crore) during the month. Bonfiglioli Transmissions was another fresh purchase during the month by the fund during October.

HDFC MF | Max Healthcare was a major purchase for the fund house in October, as it bought shares worth ₹583 crore, according to Nuvama Alternative. The other major purchases included Jio Platforms (₹523 crore), and HDFC Bank (₹442 crore). Major reductions last month included HCLTech (₹886 crore), Axis Bank (₹804 crore), and Life Insurance Corporation of India (₹434 crore). Fresh purchases were made by the fund in Triveni Turbine, PTC Industries and Shree Cement, while Gulf Oil, Laser Power, and Uniparts India were complete exits.

ICICI Prudential MF | ITC continued to be favoured by fund houses in October, with ICICI Prudential MF also making a ₹2,574 crore purchase in the stock last month. Its other major purchases included M&M (₹1,117 crore), and Bajaj Finserv (₹963 crore). It reduced its stake in Infosys (₹2,271 crore), Kotak Mahindra Bank (₹1,722 crore), and Bharti Airtel (₹1,462 crore). Fresh purchases were made in Jio Platforms, M&M Financial, Fusion Finance and Ather Energy, while GNA Axles, Atlanta Electricals, and Alivus Life Sciences were complete exits.

Kotak MF | Jio Platforms shares worth ₹690 crore were purchased by the fund house, who also increased its stake in Infosys (₹459 crore) and Adani Enterprises (₹442 crore). Major reductions were made in Bharti Airtel (₹657 crore), Coforge (₹657 crore) and Cholamandalam Investment (₹636 crore). Its fresh purchases were in Colgate-Palmolive, Fusion Finance and Wipro. It completely exited from CMR Green, Prestige Estats and Pfizer.

Axis MF | Its major additions included a purchase of shares worth ₹388 crore of Tech Mahindra, worth ₹381 crore of Ather Energy and ₹362 crore of BSE. Its major reductions comprised of a ₹194 crore sale of Torrent Power's shares, ₹171 crore worth of Pidilite's shares, and ₹156 crore worth Mankind Pharma's shares. It freshly purchased stakes in Jio Platforms and Bonfiglioli Transmission, while it completely exited from Triveni Turbine, Bharat Dynamics and SBI Funds.

data.title: Anthropic's Mega IPO Lives Up to Wall Street Hype but Fails to Revive AI Trade — WSJ
data.description:
From Wall Street's perspective, Anthropic's long-awaited stock-market debut did everything it had to: The largest initial public offering ever raised tens of billions to fund the artificial-intelligence giant's audacious plans and bestowed its early backers with eye-popping profits.

The company and its advisers pulled it off just as investors were beginning to sour on AI-related stocks, questioning whether massive, economy-shaping investments in the industry would pay off soon-and as public backlash to the sector grew. The shock resignation of Nvidia's Jensen Huang after a sex-and-spy scandal added to the market unease.

But investors big and small plowed into Anthropic's shares anyway, viewing it as a company too central to the AI universe to ignore. The shares began trading a little before noon Thursday on the Nasdaq under the ticker ANT and closed up 17%, giving the company a market value of around $1.3 trillion, or around $1.8 trillion on a fully diluted basis.

This item is part of a Wall Street Journal live coverage event. The full stream can be found by searching P/WSJL (WSJ Live Coverage).

data.title: Anthropic's Mega IPO Lives Up to Wall Street Hype but Fails to Revive AI Trade — WSJ
data.description:
By Corrie Driebusch, Kate Clark and Hannah Erin Lang

From Wall Street's perspective, Anthropic's long-awaited stock-market debut did everything it had to: The largest initial public offering ever raised tens of billions to fund the artificial-intelligence giant's audacious plans and bestowed its early backers with eye-popping profits.

The company and its advisers pulled it off just as investors were beginning to sour on AI-related stocks, questioning whether massive, economy-shaping investments in the industry would pay off soon — and as public backlash to the sector grew. The shock resignation of Nvidia's Jensen Huang after a sex-and-spy scandal added to the market unease.

But investors big and small plowed into Anthropic's shares anyway, viewing it as a company too central to the AI universe to ignore. The shares began trading a little before noon Thursday on the Nasdaq under the ticker ANT and closed up 17%, giving the company a market value of around $1.3 trillion, or around $1.8 trillion on a fully diluted basis.

The stock had opened more than 30% above the IPO price of $83, but the gains fizzled throughout the day. Some investors are already questioning if the unprofitable company can sustain its extraordinary pace of revenue growth and weather the growing threat of open-source software companies, which offer cheaper AI tools.

In another sign investors remain wary of tech and AI stocks, major indexes declined Thursday, led by the tech-heavy Nasdaq composite, which dropped 2.3%. The Dow Jones Industrial Average logged its fourth straight day of declines, losing 2.2%, or 1,101 points. The S&P 500 dropped 2% to extend its losing streak to six sessions, with all 11 sectors of the index finishing in the red.

"By any means, Anthropic's IPO was a success," said Renos Savvides, head of equity capital markets at investment-management firm Neuberger. "But this was looked at as a barometer for the AI trade, for the IPO market and for the broader market itself. By that measure, the jury is still out."

Anthropic's market debut at the Nasdaq, complete with a billboard takeover of Times Square, caps a rapid rise for a company founded in 2021 that was worth around $20 billion as recently as 2024. Its Claude chatbot and the virality of its Claude Code coding tools have propelled it to new heights, and along the way helped reshape how people work, hunt for information and learn.

Each of Anthropic's seven co-founders, a group of former OpenAI employees that includes siblings Dario Amodei and Daniela Amodei, are now worth over $20 billion apiece. The Amodeis and the other co-founders have pledged to donate 80% of their personal equity in the company to charity, in keeping with the company's avowed focus on AI safety and public benefit.

The IPO provoked a backlash from some AI safety advocates who argue Anthropic has turned its back on its safety commitments. An open letter this week called for rejection of Anthropic's "reckless attempt to amass power in the name of greater good."

Jacob Coxon, an Anthropic researcher who sparked global anxiety about AI risks when he quit Anthropic in September, appeared Thursday at a protest in front of Anthropic's headquarters to call for a ban on self-improving AI systems.

"We're here because this technology is threatening our lives," Coxon told the crowd. A protest also took place near the Nasdaq in New York.

The offering, which raised $81 billion and topped the previous IPO record set by SpaceX's June listing, will add to the massive war chest Anthropic is building to fund some $900 billion of commitments to secure computing power and data center capacity. Anthropic raised an additional $26 billion from big companies including Nvidia, Google and Advanced Micro Devices in a private placement alongside the offering.

Nearly two dozen banks worked on the IPO, with the top two, Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley, each earning fees of over $110 million.

The relatively smooth IPO — and fervent investor appetite — increases pressure on rival OpenAI, which once held the advantage, to move quickly on its own plans to go public as soon as next year.

Many on Wall Street and in Silicon Valley jockeyed for pieces of the IPO. Big institutions ranging from asset managers and hedge funds to venture-capital firms put in large orders and some were turned away.

Investing giant BlackRock received about half of the roughly $10 billion allocation it requested, according to people familiar with the matter.

Investors who bought at the IPO price were sitting on modest gains Thursday, while many early venture-capital investors in Anthropic including Lightspeed Venture Partners and Menlo Ventures reaped billions. Some individuals who bought shares at the open or shortly after the stock began trading might not be so lucky.

Ben Pfeiffer, a 45-year old entrepreneur, was sitting in his home office in New Braunfels, Texas, his eyes glued to his screen to catch the first few seconds of Anthropic trading. He had received only four of the 200 shares he requested via Robinhood, and was hoping to snap up some more. But as he watched the stock's early gains reverse soon after its debut, he decided against it.

Pfeiffer said he's still bullish on Anthropic long term — he has used Claude to build and run his business — but he's waiting for shares to drop further before buying more.

He had already thought Anthropic was "brave" for going through with its offering in this market.

"People are just really cautious right now," he said, citing recent stock declines and a string of prominent tech outages. "They're thinking 'Why would I want to invest in this technology that's making my life worse?'"

Write to Corrie Driebusch at corrie.driebusch@wsj.com, Kate Clark at kate.clark@wsj.com and Hannah Erin Lang at hannaherin.lang@wsj.com
